checks: Matched f991b5d72c5d9103 §§1–3 (1)–(8), fixing the body, mark, covariance and scalar buffer. Differentiating the ellipsoidal norm gives δΣu/G(u), and the old plane equation plus homogeneity makes the displaced vector perpendicular to the old full normal.

The uniform quadratic margin remainder changes each fiber mass only by a quadratic slab because the nearby continuous normal stays nonzero. In normalized slicing coordinates the proper derivative is linear, inside support takes the negative part, and outside support takes the positive part. Zero-area tangencies have zero derivative; d=1 retains the single-point coarea.

Pointwise density maximization gives the two support functions, and weak-* compactness gives compact convex moment sets. Difference of the support functions is exactly the derivative. Testing D and −D yields the centered absolute-moment inequality, and its converse gives the same sign condition.

If outside coarea vanishes the absolute-moment inequality forces ξ=0 almost everywhere on inside support. The proper own trace and nonzero base component at every other fiber force zero inside measure, and then the nonzero proper coarea gives the displaced centroid.

The Euclidean regular case gives the corresponding displaced centroid only when nonproper sections have zero area. This proof handles positive inside and outside supporting sections and general positive definite covariance.
